name: Latvian Pelēkie Zirņi ar Speķi (Grey Peas with Bacon)
description: Pelēkie zirņi ar speķi, Latvia's quintessential national dish, especially central to Christmas and New Year, genuinely depends on real bacon rendered first, with the onion cooked directly in that rendered fat, then folded gently into the peas so they stay whole rather than breaking apart. Real Latvian grey peas are a distinct variety; split peas stand in here as the closest reasonable approximation.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Peas, split, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt
ingredients_full.note: standing in for real grey peas

ingredients.ingredient: Peas, split, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt
ingredients.note: standing in for real grey peas

steps_detailed: Cook the bacon in a pan until the fat renders and it turns crisp, 4-5 minutes.
Add the onion to the rendered bacon fat and cook, 4-5 minutes, until softened.
Gently fold the peas into the bacon and onion, stirring carefully so they stay whole rather than breaking apart.
Warm everything together over low heat 3-5 minutes, and season with the black pepper.

name: Latvian Pīrāgi (Bacon Buns)
description: Pīrāgi, crescent-shaped yeasted buns filled with real bacon and onion, are a genuine Latvian celebration staple, real technique renders the bacon with the onion first without browning it, and the finished buns are traditionally served with a bowl of cold sour cream for dipping.
steps_detailed: Cook the bacon and onion together over low heat, 5 minutes, without browning, just to soften the onion and render the fat.
Let cool.
Mix the flour and baking powder with warm water into a soft dough.
Roll out, cut into rounds, fill each with a spoonful of the bacon-onion mixture, and fold into crescents, sealing well.
Bake at 400F (200C) for 18-20 minutes until golden.
Serve with the cold sour cream alongside for dipping - real tradition treats this as essential, not optional.

name: Latvian Cold Beet Soup (Aukstā Zupa)
description: Aukstā zupa, a cold beet soup made with real kefir, is a beloved Latvian summer staple, real technique chilling thoroughly before serving.
steps_detailed: Boil the beets until tender, 25-30 minutes, then peel and dice.
Whisk the yogurt with 0.5 cup water until smooth.
Stir in the beets and cucumber, and chill at least 1 hour.
Top with the chopped hard-boiled egg and dill before serving.

name: Latvian Rye Bread
description: Dark rye bread is Latvia's most essential daily staple, real rye flour used directly here for its genuine dense, earthy character.
steps_detailed: Mix the rye flour, baking powder, and caraway with enough water to form a firm dough.
Shape into a small round loaf and bake at 375F (190C) for 25-28 minutes until deeply golden and firm.

description: Smoked fish, especially herring or sprat, is a genuine Latvian coastal staple, real versions simply seasoned to let the smoke carry the flavor.

name: Latvian Potato Pancakes
description: Kartupeļu pankūkas, crispy grated potato pancakes, are a beloved Latvian dish, real technique squeezing excess liquid from the grated potato so they fry crisp.
steps_detailed: Squeeze the grated potato well to remove excess liquid.
Mix with the flour and egg.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry, flattening slightly, 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden and crisp.

name: Latvian Cucumber Salad
description: A simple vinegar-dressed cucumber salad, a common Latvian side, real technique salting the cucumber first to draw out excess water.
steps_detailed: Salt the cucumber slices and let sit 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Whisk the vinegar and oil together, and toss with the cucumber and dill.

name: Latvian Roasted Almonds
description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across Latvia.
steps_detailed: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

name: Latvian Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Latvian home cooking outside the specific named dishes.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.
